subject: Request: data locality controls + extended audit window for Helios Therapeutics
messages:
From: Samantha Green <samantha.green@heliostx.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data locality controls + extended audit window request

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Helios is excited about Redwood's latency/cost profile. Before we proceed to commercial terms we need to confirm a couple of security items that are blockers for our procurement and legal teams: 

1) Audit window — we require a 90-day rolling retention of audit logs and a right to perform on-site (or virtual) audits with 30 days notice but allow a one-time annual extended window of up to 14 days for evidence collection. Is Redwood able to commit to that for a private VPC deployment?

2) Data locality and KMS — logs and telemetry must remain within US regions; customer-managed KMS with no key escrow unless strictly required for incident response. Any HSM/KMS escrow would need explicit limited-scope language.

3) Support access — we need a process for managed access (jumpbox/bastion) with an approval workflow and timeboxed session recordings. No standard support staff SSH into customer networks.

4) Commercial offset — because these terms are non-standard for Private/VPC we expect some commercial concession (we're evaluating a 3-year committed instance). Please confirm what level of credit/discount you can put on the table while legal and security finalize language.

I've attached our security questionnaire and a draft mutual action plan so you can see the ask in context. Procurement is waiting for a summary of what Redwood can approve vs. what requires executive sign-off.

Can you loop in legal/ops and let me know an estimated timeline for exec approval if needed?

Best,
Samantha Green
Director, IT Procurement
Helios Therapeutics

Attachments: Helios_Security_Questionnaire.pdf, Helios_MAP_v1.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Green <samantha.green@heliostx.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Data locality controls + extended audit window request

Forwarding Helios' asks — they are a three-year committed opportunity (see deal in HubSpot). Highlights: 90-day rolling audit logs, right to audit with one annual extension window, customer-managed KMS, strict support access controls. They want a commercial concession tied to those security asks.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Legal: assess whether we can accept a 90-day audit retention + 14-day annual evidence window and draft limited-scope audit language.
- Security/Infra: confirm feasibility of US-only telemetry retention + support access controls for Private/VPC.
- Commercial: advise on credit/discount range we can offer in the Deal Desk without exec sign-off.

If we need an exec signoff I'm going to request up to a 25% one-time implementation credit (applied to first year) plus a capped SLA carveout for access window. Please advise quickly — procurement is trying to lock a sponsor call next Wednesday.

Ben
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

--- Forwarded message attached ---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Data locality controls + extended audit window request

Ben / Vivek,

Reviewed Helios' questionnaire and the MAP. High-level legal position below — this is what we can accept in contract language and where we need commercial/exec guidance: 

1) Audit rights & window
- We can agree to a 90-day retention for audit logs and provide records on request.
- The customer may request an audit; standard approach is 30 days notice and a limited-scope virtual audit.
- We cannot agree to an unlimited or on-site audit with unfettered data access. If Helios insists on a one-time extended evidence collection window (14 days), we should add: (a) scope-limitation clause that limits data types and systems in-scope; (b) Redwood will provide a named point of contact and technical runbook; (c) any on-site attendance is subject to Redwood's reasonable security and safety protocols.

2) KMS/Key management
- Customer-managed KMS is acceptable for keys encrypting customer data where technically feasible; we need to confirm with Infra which models are supported for the specific Private deployment topology.
- HSM escrow: we will not accept broad escrow. We can offer an incident-response-limited key escrow under strict attestations (time-boxed access, notarized warrants only) but that requires legal review and will be a high bar.

3) Support access
- We can implement a jumpbox/workflow and timeboxed sessions with audit recordings; however, requests for access into customer-controlled networks require prior approval and a scheduled window.

Commercial ask (requires Deal Desk/executive):
- If Helios wants the full 90-day retention + one annual extended evidence window + customer-managed KMS + support access commitments then this materially increases implementation and operational burden.
- Recommend approval for a one-time implementation credit up to 20% (first-year invoice) and an SLA exception for certain telemetry retention guarantees. Anything above 20% (or an ongoing price concession) should go to Exec sign-off.

If you want me to draft redline language for the SOW and the security addendum I can have a first pass by EOD.

Lauren
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Data locality controls + extended audit window request

Thanks for the write-up. I reviewed the asks and Lauren's note. I'm comfortable providing conditional executive approval with the following constraints: 

- Commercial concession: approve up to a 25% one-time implementation credit applied against year one ARR for the 3-year committed term, provided Helios signs within 30 days and we get an unambiguous MAP acceptance.
- Audit window: we will accept a 90-day rolling audit log retention and a one-time, 14-day evidence collection period, but the contract must include strict scope limits (systems/data types), a pre-approved checklist for evidence requests, and a mutual non-disclosure addendum for any exchanged artifacts.
- KMS: customer-managed KMS acceptable where Infra confirms no operational regression. If escrow is requested, it must be incident-response limited and subject to separate legal review; no blanket escrow.
- Support access: require scheduled sessions via our managed jumpbox with recorded sessions and privileged access review; Redwood engineers will not be granted interactive console access to customer networks outside scheduled windows.

Operational notes for Infra/Security: I expect a short runbook and estimated implementation timeline (hours and owner). If implementation exceeds 40 person-hours to implement the MAP items we should revisit the credit amount.

Ben — take this back to Helios and capture acceptance of the conditions. Legal, please prepare the redline language Lauren suggested. I'm happy to sign off on the commercial credit once we have acceptance and the MAP filled.

Vivek
Chief Revenue Officer
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Green <samantha.green@heliostx.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data locality controls + extended audit window request

Samantha — thanks for the detailed asks and for sharing the MAP. Quick summary / next steps from Redwood: 

1) Commercial: Executive approval granted conditionally for a one-time 25% implementation credit applied to year-one invoice for a signed 3-year commitment, contingent on MAP acceptance within 30 days.

2) Security terms: Redwood will accept 90-day rolling audit log retention and a one-time 14-day evidence collection period with strict scope limits; Lauren will redline the SOW and security addendum to reflect a limited-scope virtual/on-site process and mutual NDA for artifacts.

3) KMS & support access: Customer-managed KMS is supported where infrastructure permits; support access will be via scheduled jumpbox sessions, recorded and timeboxed. Any escrow requests must go through separate legal review.

Actions:
- Lauren will send draft redlines to you by EOD tomorrow.
- I will upload the updated MAP and pre-filled SOW to the DocuSign link and send for signature once you confirm MAP acceptance.
- Infra will provide a short implementation runbook and estimate; if it exceeds 40 person-hours we'll flag for revisit on credit.

Link to DocuSign (draft): https://www.docusign.com/templates/helios-redwood-deal

If that aligns with Helios, please confirm and we'll proceed with the MAP acceptance and the doc send. Happy to hop on a call with procurement this week to walk through the constraints.

Ben Carter
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Helios_MAP_v1.xlsx
